title: A Folder With No Name
body: A Midtown clerk leaves a folder on a wet bench like it grew there. Inside: a shipping window and a name that is not yours yet. The rain makes the ink look older than it is.

choices.text: Copy the window. Leave the folder.

outcomes.title: A quiet copy
outcomes.body: You keep the hour, not the paper. A week later a crate moves when it shouldn't. Nobody thanks you. The books notice.

outcomes.title: A clean errand
outcomes.body: The clerk looks at you like you failed a test and passed another. Vale would have liked the shoes. The city does not.

title: The Flats Owe Heat
body: A cousin of a cousin in The Flats has a stove that works and a landlord who does not. They ask if the Hart name is a shield or a story. The hallway smells like wet wool.

choices.text: Pay the month. Keep the stove.

outcomes.title: Warm rooms remember
outcomes.body: You leave cash that will not come back. They will mention your name at a table you are not invited to. That is how streets start.
outcomes.log: Paid a Flats stove through the month.

choices.text: The name is not a charity.

outcomes.title: A colder hallway
outcomes.body: They nod like they expected it. The stove goes out two nights later. You sleep fine. The Flats keep the receipt.

title: Harbor Lights Wants a Face
body: Mira Keene sends a boy with a note: one booth, one hour, no guns on the table. Harbor Lights is loud enough that a conversation can hide. She wants to know if you are still eighteen in the head.

outcomes.title: A booth that hears
outcomes.body: Mira talks around a ferry schedule and a man who drinks too neat. You leave with a time and no handshake. That is affection, Harbor-style.
outcomes.log: Sat a Harbor Lights booth with Mira Keene.

outcomes.title: The booth fills anyway
outcomes.body: Someone else takes your hour. Mira does not write again this year. The club keeps the music. You keep your door.

title: Ironyard After Hours
body: A foundry gate is unlocked for twenty minutes because somebody got paid to forget a key. The night shift wants a lookout who does not talk. The pay is ugly. The heat is honest.

choices.text: Watch the gate. Take the ugly pay.

outcomes.title: Ugly pay, clean exit
outcomes.body: A truck leaves heavier than it arrived. You get an envelope that smells like oil. Nobody learned your face. The sirens arrive fashionable and late.
outcomes.log: Looked out an Ironyard gate for ugly pay.

outcomes.title: A light that liked you
outcomes.body: A watchman turns a beam at the wrong second. You run. The envelope is thinner. Your name is not on a report, but it is in a mouth.

choices.text: Walk. Let the key stay forgotten.

outcomes.title: The gate keeps its secret
outcomes.body: You hear later that the truck still moved. Someone else got paid. You kept your pulse. Ironyard does not mind.

title: Westmere Does Not Invite
body: A card arrives with no stamp: a garden that is not a garden, a time that is not dinner. Westmere wants to see if your surname can sit still among old money. Bennett Lang's handwriting is too neat.

choices.text: Wear the better coat. Sit still.

outcomes.title: Old money watches
outcomes.body: You do not drink what they pour first. Lang talks about daylight surnames. You leave with a number and the sense that Westmere files people like wine.
outcomes.log: Sat a Westmere garden that was not a garden.

outcomes.title: Downtown keeps you
outcomes.body: The card blackens in a sink. Lang will say you were afraid. The Docks will say you were busy. Both can be true.
